messages:
maya: noticed a sustained p99 spike on /v1/generate starting ~02:10 UTC, p95 up ~2x and p99 up ~4x. graphs show big increase in KV cache miss rate. first saw it after the model-routing roll (canary) at 02:05. filing here to sync and triage. @oncall can you confirm impact?
jonah: on it. can you paste the query param set and a sample request id? also which region?
maya: us-west-2. sample request-id: req_9f3a2b. important bits: prompt len ~512 tokens, model variant = redwood-v1-8q, routing -> fallback to redwood-v1-8q-compat. here's the 1m log tail: ```
[02:09:58] cache miss prefix:k:12345 req=req_9f3a2b
[02:09:58] kv_fetch took=12ms key=prefix:k:12345
[02:09:58] cache miss prefix:k:67890 req=req_9f3a2b
[02:10:01] batch_exec latency=220ms model=rv1-8q
[02:10:01] cache eviction key=prefix:k:11111 policy=LRU
[02:10:02] batch_exec latency=310ms model=rv1-8q
```
jonah: hmm eviction spikes right when batch_exec latency jumps. looks like thrash — churn evicting hot prefixes. any config changes last deploy?
maya: the routing canary added compatible variant mapping + a tiny change to cache key generation (append model_variant string). that patch went in at 02:03 per deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: deploy canary 2026-03-15T02:03:21Z -> service/routing v2.7.3 deployed to us-west-2 (canary: 5%). status: success.
jonah: the cache key change rings alarm bells. if model_variant appended but other traffic still uses old key format, we could be fragmenting cache and doubling working set. that would thrash LRU. sophie / kai any thoughts on eviction policy?
sophie: LFU would be more stable under churn for prefix reuse, but we have to be careful with memory. LFU costs more bookkeeping. we can flip to tiny LFU window for 10s to stabilize.
kai: agree fragmentation + small working set increase will cause high miss rate. quick mitigation: roll back key-change or hotfix to normalize keys. also we can bump cache size by +20% and temporarily extend TTL for warmed prefixes.
maya: can we do a quick A/B: revert canary routing change in canary pool and meanwhile bump cache? which is faster?
jonah: revert canary is fastest — deploy-bot should support rollback. bumping cache requires config change + rolling restart of runtime nodes in canary — slower. rollback to previous routing version => immediate stop of key format change. recommend rollback then a cache warm-up job.
oncall: impact from SRE perspective: latencies affecting small subset of customers using long prompts; no 5xx but timeouts for some integrations hitting client-side 30s. prioritize.
maya: initiating rollback now. 
ops-bot: action: rollback requested by maya. starting rollback for service/routing in us-west-2 canary pool.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated: routing v2.7.2 restored to canary (5%). status: in-progress.
jonah: while rollback goes, capture heap + cache stats from one affected instance: `curl http://host:9090/debug/cache_stats` -> paste output here. also run `grep 'cache miss' -c /var/log/runtime.log` for last 5m.
maya: pasted below (sanitized): ```
cache_hits: 1523
cache_misses: 18470
evictions: 10234
cache_size_bytes: 450MB
max_cache_bytes: 512MB
eviction_policy: LRU
weighted_working_set_bytes: 510MB
```
jonah: wow misses >>> hits. working set > max_cache_byes -> continuous eviction. that's thrash. will wait rollback to validate.
sophie: also see that many keys are unique because of appended variant string. we should have a migration strategy: either canonicalize keys on read (normalize suffix if absent) or add backward-compat reads for both forms for a short window.
kai: code snippet we can patch quickly (runtime handler): ```python
# normalize cache key
if key.endswith('-v2'):
    base = key.rsplit('-', 1)[0]
else:
    base = key
use_key = base
``` quick diff, compile and hot-patch? risk: subtle mismatch across variants. but for immediate fix we can prefer stripping variant suffix for prefix keys.
maya: deploy-bot reports rollback to canary finished.
deploy-bot: rollback complete: routing v2.7.2 restored to all canary nodes in us-west-2.
maya: after rollback p95 back down ~1.1x baseline and p99 trending down. cache_miss rate dropped by 70% in the next 90s. 
jonah: great. next actions: 1) patch runtime to normalize keys on read (hotfix), 2) add an integration test that creates keys with/without variant suffix to prevent future regressions, 3) consider LFU or TTL tuning for prefix cache, 4) add dashboards for cache miss ratio and working set vs capacity alerts. i'll open PRs.
sophie: i'll prototype LFU small-window in staging. we'll run a 4h soak and measure hit rate.
kai: I'll draft a migration playbook: key-format changes must include a read-path compatibility for 72h and pre-warm job if format expands effective working set >10%.
maya: customer comms: some partners hit client-side timeouts; I'll coordinate with support to send a brief note and link to incident ticket #INC-2026-314.
oncall: good. tagging this SEV->near-miss. keep updates in channel. :thumbsup:
jonah: PRs: runtime hotfix -> https://repo/rt/PR/4523 (normalize keys), tests -> https://repo/rt/PR/4524 (cache-format integ), infra config -> https://repo/infra/PR/2198 (temp bump cache sizes).
maya: will monitor for 30m, removing paged oncall if stable.
ops-bot: monitoring note: p99 back within SLO; watchlist until 03:00 UTC.
maya: thanks everyone. followups: document playbook in eng-runtime/runbook/cache-format-change.md and add postmortem checklist. :eyes:
